rich_summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what happened after Bhishma’s terrible vow on the battlefield. Sanjaya describes a catastrophic phase of the Kurukshetra war: Bhishma charges the Pandava forces and devastates their army with overwhelming skill, appearing everywhere at once as his arrows slaughter warriors, elephants, and horses. The battlefield becomes a grotesque landscape of severed limbs and rivers of blood, and the Pandava troops begin to rout even in the presence of Krishna and Arjuna. Urged by Krishna, Arjuna finally confronts his grandsire. Their duel is fierce; Arjuna repeatedly cuts Bhishma’s bows while Bhishma praises his prowess. Seeing Arjuna still restrained by respect, Krishna—unable to bear the carnage—leaps from the chariot with his Sudarshana discus to kill Bhishma himself, breaking his vow not to fight, but Arjuna stops him and promises to fight with full resolve, after which the battle surges again.

highlight_spans.why: Dhritarashtra’s question frames the episode and sets up the significance of Bhishma’s terrible vow and the coming clash.
Part of the vivid battlefield imagery where bodies fall and soldiers cry out to family, capturing the emotional and human horror of the war.
The description of Bhishma’s unstoppable archery and superhuman presence, a key moment showing why the Pandava army collapses in fear.
Krishna’s explosive decision to leap from the chariot with the Sudarshana discus, nearly breaking his vow—one of the most dramatic moments of the war.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhishma standing on his chariot amid the battlefield, arrows flying from his bow in every direction while soldiers fall and the sky seems filled with shafts.
Krishna leaping from Arjuna’s chariot in fury, golden garments streaming as he charges toward Bhishma with the blazing Sudarshana discus in his raised hand.
Arjuna running after Krishna and grabbing him to stop him, the two figures frozen in tension while Bhishma waits calmly on his chariot ahead.
